lines.japanese: どの俺が署名をもらいに行きますか？
lines.english: Which of us will ask for her signature?

lines.japanese: 山科さんとは三年間同じクラスだったけれど、わりと話すようになったのは最近のことだ。
lines.english: Yamashina and I had been in the same class for three years, but we had only begun speaking with any regularity recently.

lines.japanese: 「山科さん、何してるの」
lines.english: “Yamashina, what are you doing?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、羽田君。いらっしゃい」
lines.english: “Oh, Haneda. Welcome.”

lines.japanese: あたかも私室を訪れた客でも迎えるように、山科さんはごく自然に微笑んだ。
lines.english: Yamashina smiled as naturally as if welcoming a guest into her private room.

lines.japanese: 学内でもっとも空に近いこの場所は、いま彼女の専有領域だった。
lines.english: This place, the closest point to the sky anywhere on campus, was her private domain now.

lines.japanese: 「良かったらどうぞ」
lines.english: “You’re welcome to join me.”

lines.japanese: 隣りの空席は綺麗なものだったけれど、彼女は手のひらで埃を払うような仕草を呈した。僕は礼を述べてベンチに腰を下ろす。
lines.english: The empty spot beside her was perfectly clean, but she made a show of brushing away dust with her palm. I thanked her and sat down on the bench.

lines.japanese: 「空を見てたの？」
lines.english: “Were you looking at the sky?”
“Hm? Hmm...”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは天を仰ぎながら、ひねるように首を傾けた。
lines.english: Yamashina tipped her head back toward the heavens, then tilted it thoughtfully to one side.

lines.japanese: 「もっと奥……かな」
lines.english: “Something farther in... I think.”
“Farther in?”

lines.japanese: 彼女を真似るように、首を後ろへ倒した。白く曇った幽玄の空が、厚みを忘れさせるほどにどこまでも広がっている。
lines.english: I leaned my head back to imitate her. The mystic white overcast stretched endlessly above us, so vast it made me forget that the sky had any depth.

lines.japanese: 「ていうと……宇宙？」
lines.english: “You mean... space?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだね。どちらかって言えばそうかな。光とか重力とか？」
lines.english: “Right. That’s closer. Light and gravity, maybe?”

lines.japanese: 「へえー、山科さん天文が好きなんだ？」
lines.english: “Wow. Are you interested in astronomy, Yamashina?”

lines.japanese: 「そんな高尚な趣味は持ってないよ。量子論と一般相対論の矛盾がおかしくて笑ってただけ」
lines.english: “I don’t have such lofty hobbies. I was only laughing at the contradiction between quantum theory and general relativity.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは謙遜しているようだった。たぶん。
lines.english: Yamashina seemed to be acting modest. Probably.

lines.japanese: 「よく分からないけど、なんか格好いいね山科さん」
lines.english: “I don’t really understand, but you sound cool, Yamashina.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　そうなの？　いぇい」
lines.english: “Really? Do I? Yay.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は唇の端に控えめなピースサインを置いた。
lines.english: She set a modest peace sign beside the corner of her mouth.

lines.japanese: 「ふふ、ものは言いようだね。ほんとはニュートンとアインシュタインの、子供じみた罵り合いを想像してただけなのに」
lines.english: “Hee-hee. It’s all in how you phrase it. I was actually imagining Newton and Einstein trading childish insults.”

lines.japanese: そして、話を逸らすように、視線を空から地上へ戻した。
lines.english: Then, as if changing the subject, she lowered her gaze from the sky to the earth.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君はどうしたの？」
lines.english: “What brings you here, Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん、実は山科さんに頼みがあって──」
lines.english: “Oh, right. I have a favor to ask you—”

lines.japanese: 僕は署名を集めていることについて説明した。その作品なら自分も好きだったと言って、山科さんはこころよく協力してくれた。
lines.english: I explained that I was collecting signatures. Yamashina said she had liked the manga too and readily agreed to help.

lines.japanese: そのあと昼休みが終わるまで、僕は一般相対性理論と特殊相対性理論の違いに関するレクチャーを受けて過ごした。
lines.english: After that, I spent the rest of lunch listening to a lecture on the difference between general and special relativity.

lines.japanese: ちょっとばかり頭がよくなった気がしたけれど、教室へ戻るころにはほとんど忘れていた。
lines.english: I felt a little smarter, but I had forgotten almost all of it by the time I returned to the classroom.

lines.japanese: それはそうだよね。
lines.english: That was only natural.

lines.japanese: え、俺？
lines.english: Huh, me?

lines.japanese: なんで……はあ、渉外担当だから？　はあ、それ言われちゃうと行くしかないっすけど。
lines.english: Why...? Sigh. Because I’m in charge of external relations? Well, when you put it that way, I can’t exactly refuse.

lines.japanese: 「どーもー」
lines.english: “Hey there.”

lines.japanese: ベンチに腰かけ、空の下でたたずんでいた同級生に、自然な笑顔で接近していきました。
lines.english: I approached my classmate, who sat on a bench beneath the sky, with a natural smile.

lines.japanese: 「あ、羽田君──」
lines.english: “Oh, Haneda—”
“—Haneda?”

lines.japanese: ぎくっ！　いきなり疑われてる！
lines.english: Gulp! She suspected me already!

lines.japanese: 「あ、当たり前じゃないすか。どっからどう見ても羽田君でしょ」
lines.english: “O-of course. Who else would I be? Look at me from any angle you like—I’m Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだけど……」
lines.english: “I suppose...”

lines.japanese: 言いながらも視線が訝しげです。
lines.english: Her gaze remained suspicious even as she spoke.

lines.japanese: 山科京さん。洞察力に優れたひとなのかしら。まあいいや。
lines.english: Kyou Yamashina. Was she unusually perceptive? Oh, well.

lines.japanese: 「何してたんすか」
lines.english: “What were you doing?”

lines.japanese: ごまかせ、ごまかせ。
lines.english: Cover it up. Cover it up.

lines.japanese: 「なんだろう？　空を見てたのかな」
lines.english: “What was I doing? Looking at the sky, I suppose.”

lines.japanese: テキトーな言い草です。じゃあ俺もテキトーに。
lines.english: What a vague answer. I would be equally vague.

lines.japanese: 「いっすねえ、優雅で。かっくいー。あ、座っていいすか」
lines.english: “Sounds elegant. Very cool. Mind if I sit down?”

lines.japanese: 「どうぞ」
lines.english: “Go ahead.”

lines.japanese: 彼女が軽く腰を浮かせてベンチの端へ寄ります。ぽっかり空いた一人分の間を残して、俺は逆の端へ腰を落としました。
lines.english: She lifted herself slightly and slid toward the end of the bench. Leaving one person’s worth of empty space between us, I sat at the opposite end.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうだ。ちょっとお願いがあるんすけど」
lines.english: “Oh, right. I have a little favor to ask.”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ。先に私の質問に答えてくれたら」
lines.english: “Sure. Once you answer my question.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。なんでしたっけ」
lines.english: “Uh-huh. What was it?”

lines.japanese: 「だから……君、羽田君？」
lines.english: “Like I said... Are you Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうですってば。なに言ってんすか、やだなあもう」
lines.english: “I-I told you I am. What are you talking about? Come on.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ。そう言うんじゃ仕方ないね、残念だけど」
lines.english: “I see. If you say so, I suppose it can’t be helped. That’s a shame.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そろそろ戻らないと」
lines.english: “Oh, I should be getting back.”

lines.japanese: 不意に山科京さんが、手首へ視線を落として言いました。袖口の陰から腕時計の文字盤が覗くより先に、口を開いちゃってた気もしますがね。
lines.english: Kyou Yamashina suddenly lowered her gaze to her wrist as she spoke. I had the impression her mouth opened before the face of her watch had even emerged from beneath her cuff.

lines.japanese: ま、戻りたいと仰るなら仕方ありません。このまま詮索されつづけるよりはマシですし。
lines.english: Well, if she wanted to go back, there was no stopping her. It was better than letting her keep prying.

lines.japanese: 「人見知りちゃんなのね」
lines.english: “What a shy little thing.”

lines.japanese: 息を吹きあげて前髪を揺らしました。
lines.english: I blew upward and sent my bangs fluttering.

lines.japanese: ともあれ署名は次の休み時間にでもお願いしましょう。まあ、そういう機会でもあれば。
lines.english: In any case, I could ask for her signature during the next break. Assuming the opportunity arose.

lines.japanese: ハ？　なんで俺だよ。タカシの同級だろ、あいつ。
lines.english: Huh? Why me? She’s Takashi’s classmate.

lines.japanese: いや、いいけど。行くけど。
lines.english: No, it’s fine. I’ll go.

lines.japanese: いいって。あんな風に、ひとりでボケッと空を見上げる子供は、わりと嫌いじゃない。
lines.english: I said it’s fine. I don’t mind kids who sit alone staring blankly up at the sky like that.

lines.japanese: 「おう」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese: 後ろ頭をがしがし掻きながら、ベンチの女に近づいていった。
lines.english: Scratching the back of my head, I walked up to the woman on the bench.

lines.japanese: 「あ、羽田君──」
lines.english: “Oh, Haneda—”
“—Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 微妙に疑われていた。
lines.english: There was a trace of doubt in her voice.

lines.japanese: 「あァ、そうだけど」
lines.english: “Yeah. That’s me.”

lines.japanese: 否定するわけにもいかない。俺は顎を反らせてふてぶてしく答えた。
lines.english: I could hardly deny it. I thrust out my chin and answered shamelessly.

lines.japanese: 「見んな。俺をジロジロ見んな」
lines.english: “Quit staring. Don’t fucking stare at me.”

lines.japanese: 鬱陶しい視線を避けるため、女の隣りにどっかりケツを下ろした。
lines.english: To escape her annoying gaze, I planted my ass on the bench beside her.

lines.japanese: 「あてっ」
lines.english: “Ow!”

lines.japanese: 強く座りすぎてしたたかに打った。俺はいちどケツを浮かせて、患部を撫でさすった。
lines.english: I’d hit the seat way too hard. I lifted my ass again and rubbed the sore spot.

lines.japanese: 「ってえぇ……なんだこの椅子、クソ硬ぇよ。俺のケツは意外とデリケートだっつーの」
lines.english: “Fuck, that hurt... Why is this bench so goddamn hard? My ass is surprisingly delicate.”

lines.japanese: 「おう、ねーちゃんはケツ大丈夫。こんなん座ってたらケツ痛ぇだろ。腫れてねーのケツ。ああ、あとおまえアレ、あのなんだっけ、ノイローゼの調子どう」
lines.english: “Hey, lady, your ass okay? This thing has gotta hurt. Your ass ain’t swollen? Oh, and how’s that thing—you know, your neurosis?”

lines.japanese: 女は立ちあがり、深呼吸するように両腕を天へ広げた。伸びをするために立ったのか、それとも席を立つために伸びをしたのか。どうでもいい。超どうでもいい。
lines.english: The woman stood and spread both arms toward the heavens as if taking a deep breath. Had she stood in order to stretch, or stretched in order to leave? I didn’t care. I really, really didn’t care.

lines.japanese: 「ねーちゃん。いま何してたの」
lines.english: “Hey, lady. What were you doing just now?”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　ん……べつに」
lines.english: “Hm? Nothing in particular.”

lines.japanese: やつは天を仰いだまま、振りかえらずに答えた。
lines.english: She answered without turning around, her face still raised to the heavens.

lines.japanese: 「空見てたんじゃねーの」
lines.english: “Weren’t you looking at the sky?”

lines.japanese: 「一面的にはそうだね」
lines.english: “That’s one way of seeing it.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ。暇なのな」
lines.english: “Huh. Must be bored.”

lines.japanese: 動かない背中がなにか言いたげだった。
lines.english: Her motionless back seemed to have something to say.

lines.japanese: 「君は他にすることがないときしか、空を見あげないひとなのかな」
lines.english: “Do you only look up at the sky when you have nothing else to do?”

lines.japanese: 「とは限ンねーけど、まあ、キホン暇なときだろ。そういうのは」
lines.english: “Not always, but usually you do that stuff when you’ve got time to kill.”

lines.japanese: 「そう……うん、そうだろうね」
lines.english: “I see... Yes, I suppose you would.”

lines.japanese: やつは背中の向こうで溜息をついているようだった。
lines.english: She seemed to sigh with her back still turned.

lines.japanese: 「いや、だって空ぐれー、ゆっくり見たいじゃん。余裕ねえと、どっぷり入ってけないし」
lines.english: “I mean, you wanna take your time looking at the sky, right? Can’t really sink into it when you’ve got no room to breathe.”

lines.japanese: ゆっくりと、女がようやく振りむいた。
lines.english: At last, the woman slowly turned around.

lines.japanese: 俺は後ろの金網に体重を預けてふんぞり返る。
lines.english: I leaned back against the chain-link fence and sprawled out.

lines.japanese: 「あんさ、ここって、あんたのお気に入りなんじゃねーの」
lines.english: “Hey. This is your favorite place, isn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだね。この校舎の中ではいちばん好きかな」
lines.english: “Yes. I think it’s the place I like best in this whole building.”

lines.japanese: 「俺にもあんだよ、そういう場所が。こんな青春くさい上等なトコじゃなくて、ごちゃごちゃした街ン中の、普ッ通ーの階段だけど」
lines.english: “I’ve got a place like that too. It ain’t somewhere nice and full of youthful romance like this. Just some ordinary staircase in the middle of a messy city.”

lines.japanese: 「そこに夜中ドカッと座って、空とか星とかビルとかそんなん、適当にボケッと見ンの。なんつーか、見えてる以上のモノが見えてくンだよな」
lines.english: “I drop myself there in the middle of the night and stare at the sky, the stars, the buildings—whatever. After a while, it’s like you can see more than what’s in front of your eyes.”
“...I see.”

lines.japanese: 「ま、ちょっと馬鹿みてーだけど」
lines.english: “Kinda stupid, I know.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Mm-hmm.”

lines.japanese: 「うんじゃねーよ。そこは否定しろよテメ、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Don’t agree! You’re supposed to deny it, asshole! I’ll fucking kill you!”

lines.japanese: 「なんで？　馬鹿とも呼ばれ得ない人生はもったいないと思うよ」
lines.english: “Why? I think a life that never risks being called stupid would be a waste.”

lines.japanese: なんだかめんどくさい言い回しだが、どうやら俺は誉められたようだ。そしてやつは柔らかい声で続けた。
lines.english: It was an annoyingly roundabout way to put it, but apparently she had complimented me. She continued in a gentle voice.

lines.japanese: 「で、わざわざ声をかけてくれたのは何の用？」
lines.english: “So why did you go out of your way to speak to me?”

lines.japanese: スカートの下に手のひらを挟んで、女が元の位置へ座りなおす。
lines.english: The woman tucked her palms beneath her skirt and sat back down in her old spot.

lines.japanese: ざっくり事情を説明すると、その作品なら自分も好きだったと言いそえてペンを取ってくれた。
lines.english: I gave her the short version. She said she had liked the manga too and took the pen.

lines.japanese: 山、科、京。蝋燭の火みたいにほっそりと綴られた三文字。覚えてやっても俺に害はない。
lines.english: Kyou Yamashina. Her slender handwriting traced the name like a candle flame. Remembering it wouldn’t do me any harm.
